chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan and Fadala from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about a man who rented land from another man for one thousand dirhams, then rented out part of it for two hundred dirhams. Then the owner of the land who had rented it to him said to him: 'I will enter with you in it for what you rented it for, so we will spend together, and whatever surplus there is will be between me and you.' He said: 'There is no harm with that.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a tenant to sublease part of rented land and share the profit with the landowner?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on *Muzara'ah* (sharecropping), this hadith clarifies the flexibility of contractual arrangements in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that a tenant may sublease a portion of the land and form a profit-sharing partnership with the landowner, provided the terms of cost and surplus distribution are clearly defined, reflecting the principle of *la ba'sa* (no objection) in commercial transactions.
